videos.title: AI Trade School for Healthcare
videos.description:
Stepful (YC S21) trains people for healthcare jobs, combining AI-supported learning with local hands-on training. The company trained 30,000 people last year and now works with 39 health systems, including seven of the 10 largest in the U.S. It recently raised a $55 million Series C led by Oak HC/FT.

In this episode of Founder Firesides, YC Managing Partner Diana Hu hosts co-founders Carl Madi and Tressia Hobeika where they share how cleaners losing their jobs during the pandemic sparked the idea for a faster, more affordable path into healthcare. They discuss preparing students for medical assistant jobs in five months instead of two years, using AI tutors to personalize learning, and helping hospitals train workers without asking them to leave their communities.

https://www.stepful.com

00:00 — Tackling the Healthcare Worker Shortage
03:40 — Building a Faster, Cheaper Path to Healthcare Jobs
06:57 — AI Tutors and Local Hands-On Training

videos.title: Why AI Compute Comes in Rectangles — Erik Bernhardsson, Modal
videos.description:
AI workloads don’t run in neat, three-year rectangles. But much of the GPU market still sells capacity that way. Modal CEO Erik Bernhardsson joins Latent Space to explain how Modal pools compute, scales AI workloads and thinks about the financial risks of building a GPU cloud.

Erik takes us from building Spotify’s recommendation system to founding Modal, then digs into GPU supply, alternative accelerators and the surprising growth of agent sandboxes. We also discuss sandbox security, developer experience in the age of agents, forward-deployed engineers and why Modal makes code review optional.

videos.title: AI in NYC: How Tenex Builds an AI-Native Engineering Team — Alex Lieberman & CJ Hess
videos.description:
How do you organize an engineering team when AI agents can do more of the implementation? Alex Lieberman and CJ Hess of Tenex join swyx at AI Engineer New York to discuss paying for outcomes, the MetaHarness process, enterprise AI adoption, and where AI-built software can—and cannot—replace SaaS.

They explain how Tenex keeps plans, project context and decisions in version control, discuss what gets in the way of deploying agents in companies, and debate the economics of rebuilding software. They also consider the consequences for workers and New York’s AI ecosystem.

videos.title: The Programmable Data Center — Evan Conrad, SF Compute
videos.description:
GPU compute is bought and sold like a commodity, but delivering it is a lot messier than trading a contract. Evan Conrad of SF Compute joins swyx at AI Engineer New York to explain the market they’re building—and why he thinks it needs an independent operator.

We cover:
• Why SF Compute had to build cloud operations to deliver the GPUs it trades
• How interruptions, storage and hardware generations affect compute prices
• Why batch and live inference need different contract terms
• Physical versus cash settlement, and the risk of trading a price disconnected from actual GPUs
• Why NVIDIA and the big clouds have different incentives from an independent market
• How to turn a data center into a programmable GPU cluster
